page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the FXmdsv2 family. It is configured with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The server features an x86_64 architecture and is provisioned with 168.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 84.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 472 GB disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score placing in the top tier (top 10%) and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core and parallelized workloads show significant limitations due to the single physical core configuration. Multi-core stress-ng performance and Geekbench multi-core scores are positioned in the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also indicate constraints, with large-block read-only bandwidth ranking in the bottom 10% and write bandwidth in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a highly specialized resource density, prioritizing massive memory capacity over compute scaling. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it suitable for memory-bound workloads that do not require extensive parallel processing. The tradeoff is clear: while single-threaded execution is highly competitive due to the 4.2 GHz clock speed, multi-threaded operations, database operations, and high-throughput web serving perform poorly relative to instances with higher core counts.

The FX8-2mds_v2 is designed for workloads requiring large memory footprints but minimal parallel CPU scaling. Suitable applications include memory-intensive single-threaded applications, caching layers, and lightweight database operations that fit entirely within the 168.0 GB RAM space but do not demand high multi-core throughput.
